plan.visual_reading: The arc opens on the felt ache (a guilt that will not close), lifts to Isaiah foreseeing healing through another's wounds, descends into the proof (the wounded, bruised, scourged Christ and the cross where it was borne 'in his own body'), then rises to the turn: the promise aimed at YOU, the believer healed, the cross finished at dawn, the open scarred hands, and the opening ache now closed. The cross (scene 6) is the hero bookending open and close so the Short lands on Christ.
plan.red_team_notes: Jaded Viewer risks: the stripes/scourge scenes (3,5) could blur or tip toward horror - held in Old-Master restraint, distinct framings. The 'Isaiah wrote' and 'apostle' beats are the trap (a scroll of text = Kling garbles letters) - solved by a VISION (2) and a GESTURE toward the cross (7), no writing anywhere. Scenes 1/14 are an intentional bookend; 6/9/11/12 are crucified-Christ frames in the back half - acceptable since the passage IS the cross, with varied framings (low-angle/mid/close/wide).

scenes.title: The Wound That Won't Close
scenes.purpose: Make the hook's felt ache visible.
scenes.rationale: Not a literal gory wound (horror) but the inner ache made reverent.
scenes.visible_elements: a bowed first-century man, hand over his heart, a faint dark mark beneath worn cloth, deep shadow.
scenes.subject_block: a weathered first-century Judean man seen close, head bowed low and turned away, one calloused hand pressed flat over his own chest above the heart, the rough undyed tunic worn thin where the hand rests and faintly darkened beneath it, the knuckles tight, the eyes lost in shadow, the whole figure sunk in a brown-black ground with one low shaft of light on the bowed brow
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a guilt that will not close
macro_elements: the hand pressed to the chest

scenes.title: Isaiah Sees It Coming
scenes.purpose: The point beat: 700 years early Isaiah foresaw healing through another's wounds.
scenes.rationale: Show the prophet SEEING, not writing (no scroll, Kling garbles text); a vision in shadow.
scenes.visible_elements: an aged prophet, eyes lifted, gazing toward a dim distant suffering figure; no text anywhere.
scenes.subject_block: an aged first-century Hebrew prophet seen from the side in a coarse mantle, his lined face lifted and his eyes wide upon a dim far-off rise where a single suffering figure stands bound and small against a pale bruised sky, his weathered hand half-raised in awe, the foreground rocks dark, the distance hazed in dust and prophetic light, no writing or scroll present
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of ancient foresight reaching across centuries

scenes.title: Wounded For Our Transgressions
scenes.purpose: The proof's heart: He was wounded and bruised for us.
scenes.rationale: The scourged Christ bound to the post, marked but reverent (Old-Master restraint, no gore-horror).
scenes.visible_elements: Christ bound to a low post, back marked with welts, head bowed, modest cloth, no lurid blood.
scenes.subject_block: the figure of Christ seen from behind and the side, bound by the wrists to a short rough stone post, the bare back and shoulder marked with the dark raised welts of a flogging held in solemn Old-Master restraint, the thorn-shadowed head bowed low to the chest, a modest cloth at the waist, the muscles slack and spent, warm low light raking across the marked shoulder against a deep shadowed ground
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of suffering borne for another

scenes.title: As A Lamb, Silent
scenes.purpose: OT echo (Isa 53:7, cited Acts 8:32): the silent lamb led to slaughter.
scenes.rationale: A single bound lamb, silent — the cited type, not a stretch.
scenes.visible_elements: a single young lamb lying bound and still on dark stone, eyes calm, a faint cross-shaped shadow.
scenes.subject_block: a single young lamb lying bound at the feet on a slab of dark stone, its wool pale and catching a low warm light, its eyes calm and unresisting, a thin cord at the folded legs, a faint cross-shaped shadow falling across the pale wool, the surrounding ground sunk in brown-black shadow
macro_elements: the calm eye of the lamb

scenes.title: By Whose Stripes
scenes.purpose: Macro of the stripes themselves — the lever word made visible.
scenes.rationale: Extreme close on the welt-lines, reverent and abstract, not a horror crop.
scenes.visible_elements: an extreme close of a marked shoulder and back, welt-lines raised in raking light, reverent.
scenes.subject_block: an extreme close view of a marked shoulder and upper back, the raised welt-lines of a flogging rendered in restrained Old-Master paint catching a low raking light, the skin warm and living, a single strand of dark hair fallen across, the lower edge dissolving into deep shadow, no lurid colour
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a cost counted stripe by stripe

scenes.title: In His Own Body, On The Tree
scenes.purpose: THE HERO — the gospel-pivot: Christ on the cross, the wounds that heal, the CTA landing.
scenes.rationale: Iconic, near-still, reverent crucifixion — bookends open and close so the Short lands on Christ.
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ on a rough cross, body marked with stripes, head bowed, faint light behind.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ lifted on a rough wooden cross seen from a low reverent angle against a darkening sky, the body stretched and faintly marked, the thorn-crowned head bowed in completion, a modest cloth at the waist, the arms taut along the beam, the very top of the cross bare and plain with no inscription board and no titulus and no lettering of any kind, a faint pale light breaking behind the dark hill, the small forms of onlookers dim at the foot
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of the finished work, sovereign and still
macro_elements: the grain of the cross beam

scenes.title: The Apostle Lays It On Christ
scenes.purpose: Proof: the apostle takes Isaiah's word and applies it to the crucified Christ.
scenes.rationale: Show the apostle GESTURING toward the cross (no scroll/text); the connection carried in vignettes.
scenes.visible_elements: an aged apostle, hand opened toward a dim crucified Christ beyond, soft background vignettes of the echo.
scenes.subject_block: an aged first-century apostle robed in coarse cloth seen in three-quarter, his lined face grave and certain, one open hand turned toward a dim crucified figure on a far rise beyond him, the other hand at his breast, warm light on his brow against deep shadow, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting a marked and bound back, the dark stripes of a scourge, a rough cross on a far hill, and a gathered company of the healed
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of an old promise landing on Christ
macro_elements: the open hand toward the cross
vignettes: the dark stripes of a scourge
a rough cross on a far hill
a gathered company of the healed

scenes.title: All We Like Sheep
scenes.purpose: OT echo (Isa 53:6): we all strayed; the LORD laid the iniquity on Him.
scenes.rationale: Scattered sheep on a darkening hill + one laden burdened figure — the pericope's own line.
scenes.visible_elements: scattered sheep on a darkening hillside, one shadowed figure bowed under a great weight, a far cross.
scenes.subject_block: a darkening hillside seen wide, a scattering of pale sheep wandered apart across the slope each turned its own way, and at the centre a single shadowed figure bowed low under a great unseen weight on his shoulders, the light failing to a bruised gold at the horizon, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting a strayed lamb at a cliff edge, an empty fold gate, a shepherd's dropped staff, and a far rough cross on the crest
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of the strayed flock and the weight laid on one
vignettes: a strayed lamb at a cliff edge
a far rough cross on the crest

scenes.title: He Bare Our Sins
scenes.purpose: Proof / theological centre: He bore OUR sins in His body.
scenes.rationale: Crucified Christ central, the things He bore as vignettes (no written record — abstract).
scenes.visible_elements: the crucified Christ central and dominant, soft vignettes of broken chains, a lifted yoke, bowed sinners.
scenes.subject_block: the crucified Christ at the centre and clearly dominant, the marked body bowed in completion against a dark noon sky, and faint and half-dissolved in the surrounding shadow the burdens laid on him, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting broken iron chains falling away, a heavy wooden yoke lifted from a bent back, a crowd of bowed and ashamed figures, and a dark stain washed pale
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of the great exchange borne in one body
vignettes: a heavy wooden yoke lifted from a bent back
a crowd of bowed and ashamed figures

scenes.title: The Healed Believer
scenes.purpose: Conviction: the one who receives — the old wound now closed.
scenes.rationale: Bookend echo of scene 1: the same kind of man, eased, the scar closed, light on the face.
scenes.visible_elements: a weathered man kneeling, face lifted in eased relief, an open hand at his chest where a scar has closed.
scenes.subject_block: a weathered first-century man kneeling low with his face lifted into a warm break of light, the lines of his face eased from grief to wonder, one open hand resting at his chest where a pale closed scar now sits quiet, the other hand open and empty at his side, the dark room falling away behind him into shadow
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of an undeserved healing received

scenes.title: Aimed At You
scenes.purpose: Conviction: 'ye' — the promise turned straight at the viewer.
scenes.rationale: Christ's eyes turned gently toward the viewer — the pronoun made a gaze.
scenes.visible_elements: a close reverent view of the crucified Christ's face, eyes turned gently toward the viewer.
scenes.subject_block: a close reverent view of the crucified Christ's face inclined toward the viewer, the eyes lowered yet turned with a tender willing address as if meeting one set of eyes, a thorn-marked brow, warm light catching one cheek against deep shadow, the grain of the dark beam just behind
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a promise aimed at one listener

scenes.title: Finished At The Cross
scenes.purpose: Landing: it was finished — the cross against a widening dawn.
scenes.rationale: The cross at dawn with the finished-work echoes as vignettes; gospel-frame close.
scenes.visible_elements: the cross against a widening gold dawn, the marked body still, soft vignettes of the finished work.
scenes.subject_block: the rough cross standing against a widening gold dawn, the marked body of Christ still and bowed in completion, warm light breaking from behind the upright beam across a quiet land, the hill's crest in soft shadow, subtle background vignettes fading into shadow suggesting a torn temple veil, a sealed stone, a kneeling centurion, and a far gathered church in dawn light
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of a finished work and breaking dawn
vignettes: a far gathered church in dawn light

scenes.title: Come And Receive
scenes.purpose: Landing CTA: the wounded hands open in invitation — come and receive.
scenes.rationale: Open scarred hands extended toward the viewer — the invitation made gesture.
scenes.visible_elements: the open scarred hands of Christ extended toward the viewer, palms up, nail-marks healed, warm light.
scenes.subject_block: the two open hands of Christ extended toward the viewer with the palms turned up in welcome, the healed nail-marks clear in each palm, the wrists emerging from a clean robe, warm dawn light spilling across the open hands against a soft shadowed ground, the figure beyond held gentle and out of focus
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of an open, unforced invitation

scenes.title: The Wound He Closed
scenes.purpose: Closing devotional: the ache of scene 1 now at rest — He closed it.
scenes.rationale: Direct bookend to the hook — the same man, hand fallen from a closed scar, at peace.
scenes.visible_elements: the same weathered man from the opening, now at rest, the hand fallen from a closed pale scar, soft light.
scenes.subject_block: the same weathered first-century man from the opening seen close, the head no longer bowed but lifted and still, the hand fallen open from the chest where a pale closed scar now rests untroubled, the worn cloth smooth, a soft steady light resting on the calmed face against a quiet shadowed ground
scenes.mood_block: atmosphere of an old wound finally closed

plan.rationale: Hero = the cross (6): 1 Peter 2:24 lands the healing 'in his own body on the tree', so the gospel-pivot is the cross, not the most emotional frame. Kept 4 unified scenes (7,8,9,12) carrying the NT-link and the two OT echoes (Isa 53:6 sheep, Isa 53:7 lamb) so it reads as a study, not a slideshow. Rejected every scroll/written-text scene (Kling garbles letters) for a vision (2) and a gesture (7). Bookended the felt ache (1) with its healing (14).

panel.note: The arc carries the turn: the felt ache (#1), Isaiah's foresight (#2), the wounds/scourge/cross proof (#3,#5,#6), the 'aimed at you' pivot (#11), and the finished-work landing (#12,#13,#14). Not a slideshow.

Every scene is defensible: Isa 53:5-7 + 1 Pet 2:24 + the cited lamb (Acts 8:32, #4). No invented narrative — the apostle (#7) GESTURES toward the cross rather than 'watching the scourging' (the prior A/B defect); no halos.
Back half is crucifixion-heavy (#6,#9,#11,#12) — sameness risk; mitigated by varied framing (low-angle/mid/close/wide) and the non-Christ bookend (#1/#14) + sheep/lamb OT scenes.
jesus_variant=passion set consistently on every Christ scene (#3,#5,#6,#9,#11,#12,#13); null on the man/prophet/lamb/sheep scenes. No drift.
14 scenes inside the window; subject_blocks are state-only (no motion verbs); each earns its slot; 3-5 macro_elements per scene for the cut planner.

Crucifixion is the expected image, but the honest payoff (the wounds ARE the healing; the bookend ache→closed in #1/#14) earns it. No cliché-blocklist auto-completes (no Jesus-pointing-at-self, no heaven-beam).

paper_cohesion.notes: The set coheres as one study, not a slideshow. The thread (healing through another's wounds, Isaiah 53:5 landed on Christ by 1 Peter 2:24) is carried unbroken: the felt ache opens (#1) and closes as healed (#14); the prophet sees it early (#2); the proof descends through the wounded/scourged Christ and the cross (#3,#5,#6); the apostle applies it (#7) without any invented eyewitness claim; the OT echoes are the passage's own (Isa 53:6 sheep #8, Isa 53:7 lamb #4, Acts 8:32). The 'we->ye' turn becomes a gaze (#11), and the landing lands on the cross/finished work and an open-handed invitation (#12,#13). The hero is the gospel-pivot cross (#6), bookending open and close so the Short lands on Christ. The only soft spot is a crucified-Christ cluster in the back half, which is intrinsic to Isaiah 53 and offset by framing variety and the non-Christ bookend — not a structural failure.
